title: Quiet context encoder for low-overhead SDK propagation and cold-start trace restore
creator: Amina Patel
description: Problem: SDK-injected tracing headers are a notable source of p95 overhead on serverless cold-start paths and on high-churn HTTP/UDP clients. Additionally, when a lambda or short-lived worker resumes from a frozen state we currently lose sampled upstream trace state because the header encoding is lossy under our current quick-path. Goal: Implement a compact, backwards-compatible header encoder in the SDKs that reduces wire size for common tracing payloads, carries a lightweight sampling hint that survives connection handoffs, and provides a ‘restore’ handshake to reconstruct trace context reliably on cold-started runtimes. This ticket covers design, SDK shim changes (Node/Python/Go), and a minimal runtime compatibility layer to decode legacy headers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) SDKs send new compact header X-Redwood-Ctx when enabled; legacy header X-Redwood-Trace remains supported for interoperability.
2) Header size reduced by >=40% for typical sampled traces in internal benchmark.
3) Cold-starts that receive X-Redwood-Ctx can restore span id and sampling decision with >=99% fidelity in our lab harness.
4) No increase in average request latency in our serverless testbed (p50/p95 within noise).
5) Unit + integration tests in each SDK and a compatibility decoder in runtime-1.21.
6) Documentation and a rollout plan with canary flags in console rollout UI.
notes: Design constraints: must be safe to pass through proxies/load balancers, not increase header count significantly, and respect existing baggage/otel keys. We prefer bit-packed binary payload base64-encoded into a single header for transports that strip unknown headers. Also added an escape hatch environment var REDWOOD_SDK_CONTEXT_LEGACY=true to force legacy header for customers during rollout. Consider privacy: sampling hint is a 2-bit tri-state (force-sampled, force-not, unknown) to avoid leaking high-entropy identifiers.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Amina Patel: Kickoff. Drafted spec and microbench harness. Ran initial header-size experiment: current payload avg 240 bytes, compact prototype ~130 bytes. Added sketch for 3-field payload: trace_id(8 bytes trimmed), span_id(8 bytes), sampling_hint(1 byte).

2025-02-20 - Ben Ortega: Implemented Node SDK encoder MVP in feature branch. Hooked into existing propagation middleware. Observed increased cpu by ~0.2% in warm runs, but cold-start decode adds ~1.1ms in JS runtime (needs optimization).

2025-02-22 - Lina Huang (QA): Added end-to-end test harness for cold-start restore (serverless emulator). Found edge case where header truncated by CloudFront-like proxies when size > 196 chars. Proposed base64url without padding and compacting trace_id to 64-bit by XOR-shrinking for low-contention traces.

2025-02-24 - Security review comment (J. Morales): Confirmed sampling hint design acceptable; requested threat model note: ensure we don't include customer identifiers or high-res timestamps. Asked to add the escape hatch and a slow-roll toggle in the Console. Marked security_review_required=false after review due to low risk.

2025-02-26 - Ben Ortega: Added decode path to runtime-1.21 that auto-translates X-Redwood-Ctx to internal request metadata. P50 decode latency 0.6ms native, optimized to 0.35ms after buffer reuse. Pushed updated patch to PR #1289.

2025-02-27 - Design review (S. Kim): UX for rollout flag in Console approved. Recommended showing expected traffic percentage during canary and a fallback metric indicating % of requests using legacy header.

2025-02-28 - Performance (R. Gupta): Benchmarked in serverless lab with real traffic replay. Cold-start restore fidelity: 99.3% for sampled traces, false-positive sampling decisions <0.05%. Header size reduction 45% median. Marking perf OK but asked to add a guard to detect truncated headers and fallback gracefully to legacy decode.

2025-03-01 - Amina Patel: Updated PR with truncation guard and compatibility tests across Node/Python. Added feature flag REDWOOD_SDK_CONTEXT_V1 and console rollout docs. Preparing canary deploy to 3 internal services next week.

2025-03-02 - Ben Ortega: Blocker discovered in Go SDK: base64 decoding of non-padded url variant fails on older stdlib used by nginx builder images. Added shim to accept padded and unpadded variants. Will update Go CI matrix to include older images.
